title: Targeted ads delivered 0-click exploits to install mercenary malware
gist: Citizen Lab says the AdFection campaign used targeted ads brokered by Israeli firm Discover-Tech to deliver Candiru zero-click spyware to 45 Al Jazeera devices in 2024-2025, the first confirmed ad-delivered mercenary spyware. Major ad platforms have since cut Discover-Tech off.

insights.claim: Citizen Lab reports mercenary hackers embedded zero-click exploits in ads that installed spyware on iOS and Android devices just from loading a website or opening an app, likely the first confirmed case of zero-click mercenary spyware delivered via targeted ads.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Ad-tech is now a confirmed zero-click attack vector; watch mobile security and ad-integrity vendors.
insights.locator: Researchers say that mercenary hackers laced ads

insights.claim: The AdFection campaign infected 45 devices at Al Jazeera in 2024 and 2025, and Citizen Lab warns news organizations worldwide may be actively targeted through this vector.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Media and journalist targeting raises demand for mobile forensics and threat-intel.
insights.quote: “This investigation should … serve as a clear warning signal to news organizations around the world that they may be being actively targeted via this new threat,”

insights.claim: Citizen Lab attributes the malware to Candiru (rebranded Integrity Labs): targeted ads carried JavaScript connecting to Candiru control servers, which then delivered the zero-click exploit payload.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Shows the mechanism chain from ad bid to exploit delivery; mercenary spyware vendors are adopting ad infrastructure.
insights.locator: The research lab said that the mercenary malware

insights.claim: The attacks are invisible to users unless special forensic hardware or software is run, and the report does not describe the exploited vulnerabilities, which were likely zero-days since fixed.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Detection is hard, so real infection counts are likely understated.
insights.locator: The research doesn't describe the vulnerabilities

insights.claim: Discover-Tech, an Israeli firm posing as a legitimate ad company, acts as a broker that Citizen Lab says serves as a bridge between ad vendors and the mercenary spyware ecosystem, which appears to be its primary purpose.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Identifies a specific intermediary layer between programmatic ads and spyware vendors.
insights.quote: “bridge between ad vendors and the mercenary spyware ecosystem,”
insights.locator: The ads were provided by Discover-Tech

insights.claim: Citizen Lab obtained over 4 billion bidding records showing Discover-Tech ads in over 70,000 mobile apps and more than 120,000 websites between March and June 2026.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: The scale shows how wide the exposed ad surface was.
insights.locator: Citizen Lab said it obtained more than 4 billion bidding records

insights.claim: Real-time bidding lets brokers build detailed profiles of millions of people from mobile ID, location, IP address and other data, which is what enables precise targeting of individuals.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Ad-targeting data is the enabling layer for spyware delivery, which adds regulatory pressure on data brokers.
insights.locator: The brokering involves a bidding process

insights.claim: Discover-Tech ads appeared on networks linked to NATO, United Nations, European lawmaking bodies, Australian critical infrastructure, and Norwegian and Swedish armed forces and agencies.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Government and national-security exposure may drive policy responses on ad tech.
insights.locator: Thursday's report said that Discover-Tech ad impressions

insights.claim: Google and IAB Europe had listed Discover-Tech as a certified or verified vendor, and it used GDPR consent frameworks to target EU users; Google, IAB Europe and Beeswax removed it, Google ended its ad exchange access, Vungle (Liftoff) paused access and Eskimi blocked its accounts.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Vendor-certification and consent-framework failures create reputational and regulatory risk for ad platforms.
insights.locator: Among the major vendors that listed Discover-Tech

insights.claim: Citizen Lab argues the abuse exposes structural flaws in the online advertising system, which failed to detect or prevent it.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Expect pressure for tighter ad-vendor vetting and privacy regulation.
insights.quote: “illustrates structural flaws with the online advertising system, which failed to detect or prevent the abuse documented in this report,”

insights.claim: Recommended mitigations are ad blockers, resetting the mobile advertising ID, network-level ad blocking and timely updates; the author notes it is unclear why researchers did not advise disabling personalized ads altogether.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Defensive hygiene for high-risk users such as journalists.
insights.locator: Citizen Lab called on advertisers and government officials
